|url=https://www.bharatpetroleum.in/bharat-petroleum/pdf/annual-report-2024-25.pdf|title=BPCL AR 24-25}} | website = {{official URL}} }} '''Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited''' ('''BPCL''') is an Indian [[Public sector undertakings in India|public sector]] oil and gas company, headquartered in [[Mumbai]]. It is India's second-largest government-owned [[Downstream (petroleum industry)|downstream oil producer]], whose operations are overseen by the [[Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas]]. It operates three refineries in [[Bina-Etawa|Bina]], [[Kochi]] and [[Mumbai]].{{cite web |title=About BPCL - our journey |url=https://www.bharatpetroleum.com/about-bpcl/our-journey.aspx |website=BPCL Official website |publisher=BPCL |access-date=11 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181011133503/https://www.bharatpetroleum.com/about-bpcl/our-journey.aspx |archive-date=11 October 2018 |url-status=live }} BPCL was ranked 309th on the [[Fortune Global 500|''Fortune'' Global 500]] list of the world's biggest corporations in 2020,{{Cite web|title=Global 500|url=https://fortune.com/global500/2020/|access-date=2021-05-20|website=Fortune|language=en|url-access=subscription}} and 1052nd on [[Forbes Global 2000|''Forbes'' Global 2000]] in 2023.{{Cite web|title=The Global 2000 2023|url=https://www.forbes.com/lists/global2000/|access-date=2023-05-09|website=Forbes|language=en}} == History == ===1891 to 1976=== The company, today known as BPCL, started as the Rangoon Oil and Exploration company, set up to explore the discoveries off [[Assam]] and [[Myanmar|Burma]] (now Myanmar) during the [[British Raj|British colonial rule over India]]. In 1889, during vast industrial development, an important player in the South Asian market was the [[Burmah Oil|Burmah Oil Company]]. Though incorporated in [[Scotland]] in 1886, the company grew out of the enterprises of the Chef Rohit Oil Company, which had been formed in 1871 to refine crude oil produced from primitive hand-dug wells in [[Upper Myanmar|Upper Burma]]. In 1928, [[Asiatic Petroleum Company]] (India) started cooperation with Burma Oil Company. Asiatic Petroleum was a joint venture of Royal Dutch, Shell, and Rothschilds formed to address the monopoly of [[John D. Rockefeller]]'s [[Standard Oil]], which also operated in [[India]] as [[Esso]]. This alliance led to the formation of Burmah-Shell Oil Storage and Distributing Company of India Limited. Burmah Shell began its operations with the import and marketing of Kerosene.{{cite web |title=The history and journey of BPCL |url=https://www.bharatpetroleum.com/about-bpcl/our-journey.aspx |publisher=BPCL |access-date=11 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181011133503/https://www.bharatpetroleum.com/about-bpcl/our-journey.aspx |archive-date=11 October 2018 |url-status=live }} In the mid-1950s, the company began to sell [[Liquefied petroleum gas|LPG cylinders]] to homes in India and further expanded its delivery network. It also marketed [[kerosene]], [[Diesel fuel|diesel]], and petrol in cans to reach remote parts of India. In 1951, the Burmah Shell began to build a [[refinery]] in [[Trombay]] (Mahul, Maharashtra) under an agreement with the [[Government of India]]. ===Nationalisation=== [[File:BPCL petrol filling station.JPG|thumb|left|A BPCL petrol filling station |246x246px]] In 1976, the company was nationalized under the Act on the Nationalisation of Foreign Oil companies ESSO (1974), Burma Shell (1976) and Caltex (1977).{{cite news |title=SC stays disinvestment in HPCL, BPCL |url=https://www.tribuneindia.com/2003/20030917/main1.htm |access-date=11 October 2018 |work=The Tribune |date=17 September 2003 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081202193119/http://www.tribuneindia.com/2003/20030917/main1.htm |archive-date=2 December 2008 |url-status=live }} On 24 January 1976, the Burmah Shell was taken over by the Government of India to form Bharat Refineries Limited. On 1 August 1977, it was renamed Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited. It was also the first refinery to process newly found indigenous crude [[Mumbai High Field]]. [[File:Bpcl basaveshwaranagar.png|thumb|right|BPCL petrol filling station at [[Basaveshwaranagara]], [[Bangalore]], [[Karnataka]]]] [[File:Signboard at Bharat Petroleum, RR Nagar, Bangalore (2026).jpg|thumb|right|A signboard at a Bharat Petroleum gas station in [[RR Nagar]], Bangalore]] In 2003, the government attempted to privatize the company. However, following a petition by the [[Centre for Public Interest Litigation]], the Supreme Court restrained the Central government from privatizing [[Hindustan Petroleum]] and Bharat Petroleum without the approval of Parliament.{{cite web |url=http://www.telegraphindia.com/1110304/jsp/nation/story_13665807.jsp |work=The Telegraph |title=Feather in cap for graft fighters |author=SAMANWAYA RAUTRAY AND PHEROZE L. VINCENT |date=4 March 2011 |access-date=2012-04-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110509052608/http://www.telegraphindia.com/1110304/jsp/nation/story_13665807.jsp |archive-date=9 May 2011 |url-status=dead }} As counsel for the CPIL, [[Rajinder Sachar]] and [[Prashant Bhushan]] said that the only way to disinvest in the companies would be to repeal or amend the Acts by which they were nationalized in the 1970s.{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=d4KUbiQ-9KoC&pg=PA301 |page=301 |title=Two Score and Ten: My Experiences in Government |first=G. V. |last=Ramakrishna |publisher=Academic Foundation |year=2004 |isbn=8171883397}} As a result, the government would need a majority in both houses to push through any privatization.{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZBuUNzIgJjAC&pg=PA136 |page=136 |title=Privatisation And Labour Restructuring |author=Gopal Ganesh |publisher=Academic Foundation |year=2008 |isbn=978-8171886340}} Parliament enacted the [[Repealing and Amending Act, 2016]] in May 2016, which repealed the legislation that had nationalized the company.{{cite news|title= BPCL nationalisation Act repealed in 2016; privatisation way clear|url= https://www.freepressjournal.in/business/bpcl-nationalisation-act-repealed-in-2016-privatisation-way-clear|access-date= 8 October 2019|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20191008080730/https://www.freepressjournal.in/business/bpcl-nationalisation-act-repealed-in-2016-privatisation-way-clear|archive-date= 8 October 2019|url-status= live}} In 2017, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited received [[Public sector undertakings in India|Maharatna]] status, putting it in the category of government-owned entities in India with the largest market capitalization and consistently high profits.{{cite news | url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/bpcl-gets-maharatna-status-shares-rise-over-2/articleshow/60473782.cms | title=BPCL gets Maharatna status; shares rise over 4% | date=12 September 2017 | newspaper=The Economic Times | access-date=28 December 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327095919/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/bpcl-gets-maharatna-status-shares-rise-over-2/articleshow/60473782.cms | archive-date=27 March 2019 | url-status=live }} In 2021, BPCL announced plans to invest {{currency|4.05|USD}} [[billion]] to improve petrochemical capacity and refining efficiencies, over the next five years.{{Cite web |date=May 2022 |title=Chemical Industry, Chemicals Manufacturers and Exporters in India - IBEF |url=https://www.ibef.org/industry/chemical-industry-india |access-date=2022-06-14 |website=India Brand Equity Foundation |language=en}} == Operations == Bharat Petroleum operates the following refineries: * [[Mumbai Refinery (BPCL)|Mumbai Refinery]] : Located near [[Mumbai]], [[Maharashtra]]. It has a capacity of 13 million metric tonnes per annum.{{Cite web |url=http://www.bharatpetroleum.in/EnergisingEnvironment/MumbaiRefinery.aspx?id=3 |title=Bharat Petroleum | Energising Environment | Refineries | Mumbai Refinery |access-date=8 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120919185652/http://bharatpetroleum.in/EnergisingEnvironment/MumbaiRefinery.aspx?id=3 |archive-date=19 September 2012 |url-status=live }} * [[Kochi Refineries]] : Located near [[Kochi]], [[Kerala]]. It has a capacity of 15.5  million metric tonnes per annum.{{Cite web|url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/national/integrated-expansion-project-boosts-bpclkochi-refinery/article9677392.ece|title=Integrated expansion project boosts BPCL-Kochi Refinery|date=2 May 2017 }} * [[Bina Refinery]] : Located near [[Bina-Etawa|Bina]], [[Sagar district]], [[Madhya Pradesh]]. It has a capacity of 7.8  million metric tonnes per year. This refinery started as [[Bharat Oman Refinery Limited|Bharat Oman Refinery Limited (BORL)]], a joint venture between Bharat Petroleum and [[OQ (company)|OQ company]]. Incorporated in 1994, BORL also has a single point mooring (SPM) system, a crude oil terminal (COT), and a {{cvt|937|km|adj=on}} long cross-country crude oil pipeline from Vadinar, Gujarat, to Bina, Madhya Pradesh. As of April 2021, BORL is a subsidiary of BPCL. They have a popular Loyalty Program like Petrocard and Smartfleet. {{As of|2018}}, BPCL was also setting up a [[Second-generation biofuels]] refinery at Baulsingha village in [[Bargarh district]], Odisha, of 100 kilolitre per day capacity.{{cite web | url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/energy/oil-gas/bpcl-gets-green-nod-for-rs-747-cr-ethanol-project-in-odisha/articleshow/65374612.cms?from=mdr | title=BPCL gets green nod for Rs 747 cr ethanol project in Odisha | publisher=Economic Times | date=12 August 2018 | access-date=24 November 2020}} The plant would be using 2 Lakh tonnes of rice straw to generate fuel.{{cite web | url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bhubaneswar/bpcl-to-set-up-countrys-first-biofuel-plant-at-bargarh-district-in-odisha/articleshow/66109328.cms | title=BPCL to set up country's first biofuel plant at Bargarh district in Odisha | publisher=Times of India | date=7 October 2018 | access-date=24 November 2020 | author=Singha, Minati}} In 2024, Bharat Petroleum continued to strengthen its ties with Russia, despite international sanctions imposed on Moscow following its invasion of Ukraine in 2022.{{Cite web |last=Verma |first=Nidhi |date=June 11, 2024 |title=India eyes oil deals with nations including Russia, minister says |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/india-eyes-oil-deals-with-nations-including-russia-minister-says-2024-06-11/ |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=Reuters}}{{Cite web |title=Over 1,000 Companies Have Curtailed Operations in Russia—But Some Remain |url=https://som.yale.edu/story/2022/over-1000-companies-have-curtailed-operations-russia-some-remain |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=Yale School of Management |language=en}} BPCL held discussions with Russian oil giant Rosneft to secure a long-term deal for up to 6 million metric tons of crude oil. Indian refiners, including BPCL, capitalized on discounted Russian oil, which became more appealing after Western countries halted purchases. However, these actions have drawn criticism for indirectly funding Russia's war machine. While BPCL's officials acknowledged narrowing discounts on Russian oil and potential challenges in exceeding price cap thresholds, the company remains poised to utilize up to 40% Russian crude in its refineries. It involves maintaining controversial partnerships with Russia during its ongoing aggression against Ukraine.{{Cite news |date=2023-07-27 |title=BPCL still in talks for Russian oil deal, discounts narrow |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/energy/oil-gas/bpcl-still-in-talks-for-russian-oil-deal-discounts-narrow/articleshow/102166625.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2024-12-27 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} == Subsidiaries == '''[[Indraprastha Gas|Indraprastha Gas Limited]]''', a [[joint venture]] between [[GAIL|Gas Authority of India Limited]] (GAIL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited, and the [[Government of Delhi]] to operate the Delhi City Gas Distribution Project. '''[[Petronet LNG]]''', a joint venture company promoted by the [[GAIL|Gas Authority of India Limited]], [[Oil and Natural Gas Corporation]] Limited, [[Indian Oil Corporation]] Limited, and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited to import LNG and set up LNG terminals in the country. '''Bharat Renewable Energy Limited''', a joint venture company promoted by BPCL with Nandan Cleantech Limited (Nandan Biomatrix Limited), Hyderabad, and Shapoorji Pallonji Group, through their affiliate, S.P. Agri Management Services Pvt. Ltd, specializes in offering Bio diesel plants, ethanol, bio-diesel plants, [[Millettia pinnata|Karanj (Millettia pinnata)]], [[Jatropha]] and [[Millettia pinnata|Pongamia (Pongamia Pinnata)]] plantation services, renewable generation services, etc. In 2013, Shapoorji Pallonji Group exited the joint venture.{{Cite news|last=Pathak|first=Kalpana|date=2013-09-23|title=Shapoorji Pallonji to exit renewable energy venture floated with BPCL|work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/shapoorji-pallonji-to-exit-renewable-energy-venture-floated-with-bpcl-113092300171_1.html|access-date=2021-05-03}} '''Bharat PetroResources Limited''', a wholly owned subsidiary of BPCL. ==Joint ventures== *[[Maharashtra Natural Gas Limited]] is a joint venture of GAIL and BPCL. *Haridwar Natural Gas Pvt. Ltd., a JV of BPCL and Gail Gas Ltd. ==Ownership== The cabinet had cleared a plan to sell 53.3% of its stake in Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL){{citation needed |date=November 2022}} with the rest owned by Foreign Portfolio Investors (13.7%), Domestic Institutional Investors (12%), [[Insurance]] (8.24%), and the balance held by individual shareholders.{{Cite web |title=Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd financial results and price chart - Screener |url=https://www.screener.in/company/BPCL/consolidated/ |access-date=2022-08-30 |website=www.screener.in}} But as of 2024, such a plan is said to be off the table.{{cite web | url=https://www.businesstoday.in/india/story/modi-30-bpcl-privatisation-completely-off-the-table-high-revenue-psus-need-not-be-sold-says-hardeep-singh-puri-432868-2024-06-11 | title=Modi 3.0: BPCL privatisation completely off the table, high revenue PSUs need not be sold, says Hardeep Singh Puri | date=11 June 2024 }} == Plans of Disinvestment == On 21 November 2019, the [[Government of India]] approved the privatization of Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited.{{Cite news|title=Privatisation push: Cabinet approves strategic sale of BPCL, 4 other PSUs|newspaper=Business Standard India|date=21 November 2019|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/economy-policy/privatisation-push-cabinet-approves-strategic-sale-of-bpcl-4-other-psus-119112100076_1.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191123074254/https://www.business-standard.com/article/economy-policy/privatisation-push-cabinet-approves-strategic-sale-of-bpcl-4-other-psus-119112100076_1.html|archive-date=23 November 2019|access-date=23 November 2019|last1=Roychoudhury|first1=Arup}} The government invited bids for the sale of its 52.98% stake in the company on 7 March 2020.{{cite web|title=Govt invites bids for BPCL, to sell full 52.98% stake in company|url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/govt-invites-bids-for-bpcl-to-sell-full-52-98-stake-in-company-5012761.html|access-date=7 March 2020|website=Moneycontrol|date=7 March 2020 }} The Government decided to consolidate the businesses of BPCL before privatization, starting with the Numaligarh Refinery Ltd. (NRL). The Government decided to keep Numaligarh Refinery Ltd. (NRL) in the public sector, honouring the Assam Peace Accord. In March 2021, Bharat Petroleum Corporation sold its entire 61.5% stake in Numaligarh Refinery in Assam to a consortium of [[Oil India|Oil India Ltd.]], [[Engineers India|Engineers India Ltd.]], and [[Government of Assam]] for ₹9,876 crore.{{Cite web|title=BPCL offloads entire 61.5% stake in Numaligarh Refinery for Rs 9,876 crore|url=https://www.businesstoday.in/sectors/energy/bpcl-offloads-entire-615-stake-in-numaligarh-refinery-for-rs-9876-crore/story/435034.html|access-date=2021-05-03|website=www.businesstoday.in|date=26 March 2021 }} BPCL also acquired a 36.62% stake in Bharat Oman Refineries or Bina refinery situated at Bina in Madhya Pradesh, India from [[OQ (company)|OQ company]], for ₹2,400 crore. BPCL has been holding 63.4 per cent and OQ 36.6 per cent equity in the company. The Government of Madhya Pradesh has a minor stake in the company through compulsorily convertible warrants. With the acquisition of OQ's entire stake in BORL, BPCL will establish control over BORL.{{Cite web|title=India's Bharat Petroleum buys OQ's entire in Bina refinery|url=https://www.hydrocarbons-technology.com/news/bharat-petroleum-oqs-bina-refinery/|access-date=2021-05-03|website=www.hydrocarbons-technology.com|date=31 March 2021 }}{{Cite web|title=BPCL Acquires Oman's 36.6% Stake In Bina Refinery|url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/companies/bpcl-acquires-omans-36-6-stake-in-bina-refinery-6715321.html|access-date=2021-05-03|website=Moneycontrol|date=31 March 2021 }} The Indian Government attempted to sell BPCL during fiscal year 2021–2022.{{Cite web |last=Moneycontrol News |date=17 November 2021 |title=Govt will privatise 5-6 companies in 2021-22, including BPCL: DIPAM Secretary |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/economy/govt-will-privatise-5-6-companies-in-2021-22-including-bpcl-dipam-secretary-7730871.html |access-date=2022-05-07 |website=Moneycontrol |language=en}} However, the sale of BPCL has been pushed to fiscal year 2022–2023, and it has been reported that the Government is building a new strategy for the sale of the company.{{Cite web |last=Batra |first=Shubham |date=5 May 2022 |title=Why Modi govt's BPCL privatisation process ran out of gas and is back to the drawing board |url=https://theprint.in/economy/why-modi-govts-bpcl-privatisation-process-ran-out-of-gas-and-is-back-to-the-drawing-board/942568/ |access-date=2022-05-07 |website=ThePrint |language=en-US}} In addition to this, it has also been reported that rising oil prices, along with increasing development and use of green energy, is leading to delays in the privatisation process.{{Cite web |last=Aulakh |first=Gulveen |date=2022-04-22 |title=Centre weighs going back to drawing board on BPCL sale |url=https://www.livemint.com/news/india/centre-weighs-going-back-to-drawing-board-on-bpcl-sale-11650649334170.html |access-date=2022-05-07 |website=mint |language=en}} On June, 12 2024, the Petroleum Minister of India informed that any plans of disinvestment is off the table.{{cite web | url=https://www.businesstoday.in/india/story/modi-30-bpcl-privatisation-completely-off-the-table-high-revenue-psus-need-not-be-sold-says-hardeep-singh-puri-432868-2024-06-11 | title=Modi 3.0: BPCL extract: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) is an Indian public sector oil and gas company, headquartered in Mumbai. It is India's second-largest government-owned downstream oil producer, whose operations are overseen by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. It operates three refineries in Bina, Kochi and Mumbai. BPCL was ranked 309th on the Fortune Global 500 list of the world's biggest corporations in 2020, and 1052nd on Forbes Global 2000 in 2023.
